messages:
ivy (Customer): hey @sara we started seeing a wave of 504s and partial streaming failures around 09:30 PT. Clients end up in SDK retry loops. Happening across multiple tenants. attaching sample logs below

sara (Support): sorry about that, ivy. can you confirm sdk + node/python version and a minimal repro? are these streaming uploads or single-request bodies?

ivy (Customer): node v18 + redwood-sdk 1.4.2. streaming audio chunks (~1.2MB/session) over HTTP/2. trimmed log: ```2026-03-17T09:31:02Z ERROR request id=abcd1234 status=504 message="upstream read timeout" sdk_retries=3 write_err=EAGAIN socket_buf=0``` also client shows repeated "write stalled, retrying" messages.

sara (Support): thanks. tagging @mike @dan to triage. any infra alerts?

mike (Oncall): I'm seeing a spike in ingress queue length on edge-proxy-usw2 and p95 tail latencies up. opening triage.

deploy-bot: incident #INC-493210 opened; severity=high; link=https://redwood.incidents/INC-493210

dan (SRE): initial hypothesis: client slowwrite/egress throttling -> upstream connection backlog -> gateway gives up (504). can you run a quick curl test to see if a single-body request stalls on send? also what's concurrent stream count?

ivy (Customer): concurrency ~40 concurrent sessions. curl -v to the same endpoint returns: "* Connected to api.redwood.example (10.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/2
> [100% data sent]
* TLS handshake complete
< HTTP/2 504
" plus tcpdump showing many "sndbuf full"/"no space" kernel lines. snippet: ```12:31:04.123456 IP client > proxy: Flags [P.], seq 1:1300, ack 1, win 0, options [nop,nop,TS val 123456 ecr 654321]```

dan (SRE): repro steps we ran locally: 1) start node redwood-sdk 1.4.2 client with 50 concurrent streaming sessions 2) simulate limited egress: `tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 200kbit burst 32k latency 400ms` 3) observe proxy backlog growth and backend connection resets -> 504 spam. commands we used: ```# throttle egress to emulate slowwrite
tc qdisc add dev lo root tbf rate 200kbit burst 32k latency 400ms
# run concurrency test
node load_test.js --concurrency 50 --chunk-size 64k
``` saw gateway logs: "proxy: conn backlog exceeded; resetting backend" and client-side: "write EAGAIN -> retry"

sara (Support): suggested immediate mitigations: 1) reduce client concurrency (sdk config: maxConcurrency=8) 2) enable smaller chunking (max_chunk_size=64KB) 3) temporarily route traffic to dedicated pool (we can flip this for you) 4) turn on client-side bounded queueing to avoid creating head-of-line blocking. want us to switch the route now?

ivy (Customer): please route to dedicated pool, that'd be great. also would like ETA on firewall/edge config changes if you plan to adjust socket buffers.

mike (Oncall): routing to dedicated pool for tenant started at 09:56 PT. also rolling small ingress config: increase tcp_rmem/tcp_wmem limits on edge nodes and bump keepalive timeout. roll in progress; ETA ~45m. will monitor metrics.

ivy (Customer): retested immediately after routing, errors dropped to 0 for ~10m while I ran sanity tests. thanks. keeping watch and will report if anything flares.

dan (SRE): long-term actions: - add guidance in SDK for backpressure-aware send throttling + jittered backoff - add server-side defensive per-connection sliding-window to avoid one slow client stalling whole backend - chart ingress queue length and surface alert earlier. I'll open follow-up tickets and PRs.

sara (Support): we'll update your support ticket with the mitigation steps and ETA on config rollout. thanks everyone for the quick triage :thumbsup:
